project.title: 面向飞机 B-Rep 模型小特征处理的可追溯图学习与几何重建框架
project.target_venue: Journal of Computational Design and Engineering (provisional)

artifacts.path: ../飞机STEP模型小特征识别期刊论文逻辑大纲_按意见修订_最终版.docx

contract.gap: Existing CAD feature-recognition work provides limited evidence for traceable, risk-sensitive small-feature recognition and downstream geometry processing on complete heterogeneous aircraft B-Rep models.
contract.task: Recognize rivets and other surface-features at B-Rep face level, preserve face identifier traceability, and validate safety-aware downstream CAD removal and reconstruction.
outcomes: per-aircraft error and background false-positive analysis
traceable CAD removal and geometry reconstruction
optional mesh and CAE impact validation

questions.text: Can face geometry and adjacency topology support rivet and surface-feature recognition across complete aircraft models?
Does independent dual-specialist encoding reduce task interference relative to a unified classifier?
Can smooth-shell protection reduce high-risk background false positives without unacceptable true-feature loss?
Can predictions remain traceable to original B-Rep faces and support auditable geometry removal and reconstruction?

contract.contribution: A traceable, risk-sensitive graph-learning and CAD geometry-processing framework for small features in complete aircraft B-Rep models.
nonclaims: No universal generalization claim across all aircraft or CAD sources.
BRep validity alone does not establish geometry or physics equivalence.
No CAE acceleration or response-preservation claim before controlled downstream experiments.
Human visual review is not described as fully automatic validation.
Retired BFS and 51-dimensional experiments are not part of the formal model.

semantic_locks.canonical: background=0, rivet=1, surface_feature=2; decal and window provenance remains in JSON
Dataset partitioning is performed by complete aircraft model, not by randomly splitting faces
Do not use a 0.0005 normalized-area hard prediction filter because valid large surface-features exist

terminology.concept: surface target class in manuscript prose

style_profile.language_variant: British English for manuscript; Simplified Chinese for planning

facts.value: 48 node features, 6 edge attributes, 4 layers, hidden dimension 64, seed 123, 50 epochs, rivet threshold 0.9, surface threshold 0.5

alignment.method: B-Rep face graph with geometric and topological attributes
alignment.evidence: Frozen complete-aircraft evaluation and face-level overlays
alignment.result: On 34162 faces from nine aircraft after complete post-processing, rivet F1=0.9394 and surface-feature F1=0.5172; Airbus contributes 713 of 818 background false positives
alignment.interpretation: Face-level recognition is feasible in the reported partition but performance varies substantially by class and aircraft
alignment.limitation: Some test aircraft may have been used during historical development; limited aircraft and CAD-source diversity

alignment.method: Dual-specialist GNN versus unified three-class baseline
alignment.evidence: Single-seed parameter-matched controlled retraining on the fixed 17/9 partition
alignment.result: Dual specialist: 599188 parameters, mIoU 0.4251, macro F1 0.5270, background FP 4048; unified: 596884 parameters, mIoU 0.4180, macro F1 0.5200, background FP 4936
alignment.interpretation: The dual-specialist run improved rivet and background-risk measures, whereas the unified run had higher surface-feature F1; no uniform or statistical superiority claim is supported
alignment.limitation: One seed only; repeated runs are required for uncertainty estimates

alignment.method: No constraints versus topology versus topology plus visibility versus complete post-processing
alignment.evidence: Cumulative face-level ablation on all 34162 fixed-test faces
alignment.result: Background FP changed 4152 -> 1262 -> 944 -> 818; surface-feature F1 changed 0.4916 -> 0.4916 -> 0.5576 -> 0.5172
alignment.interpretation: Topology and visibility provide most of the gain; the complete conservative stage further reduces false positives but sacrifices surface-feature recall
alignment.limitation: Guard parameters may be domain dependent

alignment.method: face identifier traceability, CAD removal, local reconstruction, and BRep checks
alignment.evidence: Nine final B-Rep models plus quantitative geometry validation
alignment.result: Nine original--simplified pairs were compared under fixed surface-meshing settings; median triangle reduction 17.84 percent and median meshing-time reduction 43.00 percent; operation-level success inventory remains pending
alignment.interpretation: The reported pairs show changes in CAD and mesh properties, without establishing removal completeness or engineering-response equivalence
alignment.limitation: BRep validity does not prove physical equivalence

decisions.decision: Plan the paper as an end-to-end recognition and geometry-processing framework, with a recognition-only fallback title if downstream evidence remains insufficient.
Treat the 3631-face evaluation as historical because it does not match the current 34156-face candidate test CSV.
By author instruction, describe the study in terms of B-Rep models and face identifier traceability, without presenting STEP as a file-format contribution.
By author confirmation, use the current 17-aircraft training and 9-aircraft test partition as the fixed evaluation dataset; the earlier dataset-scope mismatch is resolved.

By author instruction, organize related work from three-dimensional scene segmentation to CAD feature recognition, then state the bounded gap for learning-guided small-geometry processing in industrial simulation workflows; do not claim mesh or simulation effects without controlled evidence.

By author instruction, introduce concise B-Rep preliminaries before the learning formulation, treat small geometry only as a supervised label contract, and make face-graph encoding and dual-specialist graph learning the theoretical focus of Section 3.

By author instruction, present Chapter 4 as a concise traceable processing contract: retain candidate filtering principles, staged face identifier handling, operation alternatives, rollback, and B-Rep checks, but do not enumerate detailed boundary-case rules in the main text.

By author instruction, organise the experimental evidence into training and face-level recognition (6.1), CAD simplification with original--simplified surface-mesh comparison (6.2), and cross-aircraft variation with evidence boundaries (6.3); do not fabricate a training-convergence curve when epoch-wise records are unavailable.

For the current integration revision, report the observed recognition and surface-mesh results in the abstract and conclusion, and describe the fixed nine-aircraft partition as developmental because historical use of some test aircraft remains possible.
